chunks: How to drive an inductive load. The question: How do you drive an inductive load?
A motor, solenoid, or relay coil is an inductor, which resists any sudden change in its current.
The simplest safe way to drive one is a MOSFET switch between the load and ground, controlled by a microcontroller pin.
Always add a flyback diode across the load, so the current has somewhere to go when the switch opens. You vary speed or hold force with PWM.
Size the switch for the starting surge, not the running current.
Picture a heavy truck that cannot stop instantly. A runaway-truck ramp gives it somewhere safe to slow down. The coil's current is the truck's momentum.
The switch opening is the brake. The flyback diode is the escape ramp. Without one, it hits whatever is ahead: the MOSFET.
The standard low-side drive. D 1 across the load (cathode to V S ) is reverse-biased while Q 1 is on and takes over the inductor current when Q 1 turns off.
R g tames gate ringing and limits GPIO current; R pd keeps Q 1 off when the pin floats.
MOSFET: a transistor used as a fast electronic switch. Flyback (freewheel) diode: a diode across the load that carries the coil's current after the switch opens.
Inrush / stall current: the big current at start-up or when stuck, V over R , because a still motor makes no back-EMF (opposing voltage).
PWM duty cycle: in PWM the switch flips on and off rapidly. The fraction of time on sets the average voltage.
Time constant: L over R , the time for the coil's current to fall to about 37% of its starting value.
A 24 volts solenoid coil of 24 ohms and 100 millihenries draws 1 amps, and stores 1 over 2 times 0. 1 times 1 squared equals 50 mJ.
When the MOSFET turns off, the diode catches that current. It decays with a time constant of 0. 1 over 24 equals 4. 17 milliseconds, falling from 1 amps to 0. 1 amps in about 9.
6 milliseconds. To hold the plunger cheaply, run PWM at 33% duty: the average is 8 volts, so it holds with about 0. 33 amps instead of 1 amps. That is the whole idea.

"I'd use a logic-level N-MOSFET as a low-side switch with the load between the supply and the drain, a gate resistor and pull-down, and a flyback diode across the load so the inductor current has a path when the FET turns off.
Size the FET for voltage margin and stall or inrush current, then use PWM for speed or hold current.
For two directions or protection and diagnostics, step up to an H-bridge or a driver IC."
